terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: ONE BAY of a modular outdoor roof kit, the thick-thatch member of the set: a 4 x 4 m cell on a 4 m grid, so a canopy grid lands two by two on the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles. Nothing opens, turns or swings and nothing attaches -- a neighbouring bay is PLACED at 4 m, not socketed -- so one root pivot at base-center and zero sockets. Open on all four sides. Resort salas, temple rest shelters and roadside pavilions across the north-east; laid thick and re-ridged every few years. Vetiver bleaches silver-grey on the weather face and stays warm straw in the shade, and green moss gathers where the roof stays damp.

reasoning: ONE timber merge -- four posts, four head plates, eight knee braces, two king posts, the ridge beam, six rafters, FOUR raking barge boards and eight cord lashings; ONE thatch merge carrying both slopes, the ridge roll and seven binding collars; ONE InstancedMesh of eight purlins: THREE draw calls of 4.

Two materials of three: sawn honey timber (vertex colours -- post, plate, barge, rafter, cord) and vetiver thatch (vertex colours -- thatch and binding cord). Both textureless, each with one post-construction canvas.

The seven ridge bindings were FOLDED into the thatch merge rather than instanced. Instancing saves 120 triangles and costs a fourth draw call on a ceiling of four; at 1,864 of 4,000 the triangles are the cheap axis and the submission is not.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, no declared collider shape, no destruction groups.

specDepthDecision.rationale: At distance the identity is a thick grey-green thatch bell with a bound ridge and two raking barge boards; close up it is the combed course structure and the cord bindings over the roll. The notes forbid modelled stems, so the courses are a canvas and the mass is in the 260 mm bed and the convex rake.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The GABLE IS OPEN. The plate fills both gables with a thatched tympanum framed by the barge boards, and it is the most distinctive thing on the plate after the roof -- but the registry notes say "Open on all sides -- no walls, no infill", and a tympanum is infill. The notes are the module contract and the plate is the material and detail reference, so the tympanum is not built and the truss shows through instead, as on every other bay in the set.
The roof stops ON the module edge rather than overhanging it: a 4 m grid bay that overhangs collides with its neighbour.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 4.00 x 3.90 x 4.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; none collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.
actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center, +Y up, the ridge along X. A neighbouring bay sits at +-4.00 m on X or Z with the same alignment, and the two bays' corner posts then pair at the shared edge.

silhouette.description: A 4.00 x 4.00 m bay: four 160 mm posts at the corners carrying a head frame at 1.97-2.14 m with eight knee braces, and above it a thick gable with its ridge along X -- 260 mm of vetiver from a 2.25 m eave to a 3.75 m apex on a convex rake, a 300 mm bound ridge roll topping out at 3.90 m with seven cord bindings, and a raking barge board on each of the four rake lines. Open on all four sides.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: z spans exactly -2.000..+2.000 at the thatch eaves and x -1.998..+1.998 at the raking barge boards, so the two axes have DIFFERENT owners and no bounding-box face is shared with another component -- which is what check-coplanar is measuring when it reports same-facing pairs. The thatch verge stops at 1.88 and the barge boards run 1.89 to 1.99 outboard of it; the barge boxes are rotated onto the rake, so their length was set from the AABB arithmetic (half-z = L/2 cos s + h/2 sin s) rather than from the rake itself. y 0.000 to 3.900 at the top of the ridge binding, which is 8 mm proud of a 150 mm ridge roll whose centre is therefore at 3.742. A silhouette scan of the plate settles the pitch: apex at row 96, ground at row 927 and the near gable's eave corner at row 462, so the EAVE SITS AT 0.56 OF THE HEIGHT AND THE ROOF IS 44% OF THE PROP -- the proxy's 0.50 was right and the notes' 2.40-over-3.30 was not. With the 4 m span fixed by the grid, eave and ridge together over-determine the pitch, and the height is the only one of the three the module contract does not constrain, so the height is what moved: 3.30 -> 3.90 with the eave at 2.25, which keeps walk-under clearance, puts the eave at 0.577 H and rakes at 36.9 degrees against the first build's 20.7. Proxy (Meshy v7): w:h:d 1 : 1.015 : 1.007, a near cube, post grid 0.724 x 0.860 H, roof reaching 0.965 x 0.916 H at an eave sitting at 0.50 of the total height -- the roof is HALF the prop, which is what the notes mean by steeply gabled. The first build read the notes as fixing BOTH ends and built it at 27% and 20.7 degrees, carrying the steepness on a 260 mm bed and a convex rake instead -- which is the STRAW DUMPED ON A FRAME the notes themselves warn against. The plate scan agrees with the proxy, so the height moved and the roof is built at 44% and 36.9 degrees; the thick bed and the convex rake are still there, on top of a pitch that is now right. Post section 0.16 from the proxy's post-grid columns.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: w:h:d 1 : 1.015 : 1.007, post grid 0.724 x 0.860 H, roof 0.965 x 0.916 H, eave at 0.50 H. Used for the post section and for confirming that the roof is the dominant mass. NOT used for the eave height or the pitch: the notes fix both, and honouring them halves the roof's share of the height. The plate also shows a THATCHED GABLE TYMPANUM which is deliberately not built -- see assumptions.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: the bay is symmetric about both axes and open on all four sides; the plate shows one gable end and one full slope, which between them cover every distinct elevation.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-timber (0.88) at #9b8368 sd 23 and region-barge (0.84) at #7c5f3f sd 41 -- warmer and newer than the nipa bay's silver-brown, R minus B around 50 to 60.

AUTHORED AS THE INVERSE OF THE HARNESS TRANSFER using the two-point solve probed on the nipa module (authored luma 147.5 rendered 66 and 220.5 rendered 180 on the same vertical post face). Carried at #dcc8a0 with post #d2bfa0, plate and brace #e0d0b4, barge #eaddc6, rafter #c5b096 and cord #9a8058 as vertex colours. Measured back at 144 / 117 / 117 / 105 across the four azimuths against a backdrop of 58. The first build was authored a step more saturated and rendered R minus B 91 against the plate's 70, so the whole set was pulled toward neutral at constant luma.
Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px sawn-timber multiply canvas after construction, world UVs at 0.60 m.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-vetiver (0.90) at #958e7c sd 38, region-eave (0.86) at #999084 and region-ridge (0.86) at #c2b4a5 -- SILVER-grey, R minus B only 18 to 29, against the nipa bay's warm straw. region-straw (0.82) at #8e6e49 is the shaded face and is 40 warmer, which is the tonal range the tile's course spread carries.

The first build authored this as warm as the nipa thatch and rendered R minus B 47 against the plate's 18; re-authored neutral at the same luma and measured back at 167 on the sunlit slope against the plate's 151-171.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px thatch multiply canvas after construction, world UVs at 1.70 m -- SEVEN courses per tile (0.24 m per course) of 620 hairline stems 1-2 px wide at a 0.10 tonal spread and an almost straight butt, which is combed grass; the nipa bay's tile is five courses of 170 broad 3-7 px blades at 0.20 spread with a deeply ragged butt. Nine moss patches multiply green in, because the tile is a multiplier over a pale albedo and a multiply can only darken -- moss has to arrive as less red and blue, never as painted green.

A silhouette scan of the plate settles it against the notes and with the proxy: apex row 96, ground row 927, near-gable eave corner row 462, so the eave sits at 0.56 of the height and THE ROOF IS 44% OF THE PROP against the 27% built. The height is the only one of the three the module contract does not constrain, so the height is what moved: 3.30 -> 3.90, eave 2.25, 36.9 degrees, walk-under clearance kept and the 4 x 4 plan untouched.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 1,864/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases. Open on all four sides: turntable with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement and a holeviz read per azimuth showing red over the gable voids and brace bays only.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components plus one repetition system: 3 of 4.

materials.note: timber and thatch: 2 of 3. Post, plate, brace, barge, rafter and both cords are vertex colours.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1,864 of 4,000: 544 in the frame merge (38 boxes), 1,180 in the thatch (an 18 x 14 grid with edge strips, a 12-segment ridge roll and seven open collars), 140 in eight purlin instances.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes throughout the frame, rotated onto the 45 degree braces and the 36.9 degree rake; the roof is a height grid with thickness, the ridge a cylinder and the bindings open partial cylinders.
One InstancedMesh of eight purlins. In a scene the HOST places whole bays on the 4 m grid.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Both materials are declared textureless. Two 512 px canvases after construction, ~2 MB of texture VRAM.

risks.description: The plate fills both gables with a thatched tympanum framed by the barge boards; the build leaves them open.
risks.mitigation: The registry notes say "no walls, no infill" and a tympanum is infill. Recorded in assumptions with the reasoning; the barge boards, which are the other half of what makes that gable read, ARE built.

risks.description: The notes fixed eave 2.40 AND ridge 3.30, which over-determines the pitch on a span the grid fixes at 4 m, and gave 20.7 degrees.
risks.mitigation: Settled by measurement rather than by precedence -- a plate silhouette scan puts the eave at 0.56 H and the roof at 44% of the prop, agreeing with the proxy against the notes. Declared height corrected to 3.90 with the arithmetic in notes; the plan stays exactly 4 x 4 and the grid contract is untouched.

risks.description: The derived collider compound loses the ledge at y 3.1 -- the 1 m2 top of the bound ridge roll -- because no compound box reaches within 0.10 m of a 300 mm cylinder's crown. 7 of 8 ledges preserved, coverage 0.9926.
risks.mitigation: Above the 0.95 the gate asks for, and the lost ledge is the apex of a thatched ridge: nothing in the game stands on it. Recorded rather than forced by adding a ninth part to a compound already at its ceiling of 8.

risks.description: Open on all four sides, so the volume under the roof and both gable voids are background enclosed by the silhouette.
risks.mitigation: Turntable run with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement and a holeviz read per azimuth; every timber and thatch face measured off the backdrop band first, darkest 105 against 58.
